title: The Museum Heist
briefing_md:
On Monday at 9 AM, curator Fatima Sheikh opened the City Heritage Museum and found the glass case of the Maharani's Emerald Necklace perfectly intact, with a necklace inside. But tests proved it was a fake.

No alarm rang, no glass broke, and the case was locked. On Sunday evening the museum had hosted Heritage Night, a party for donors.

Three people are being talked about:
• Joseph Pinto, 47, the night guard. He says he did his rounds and saw nothing.
• Rekha Bhandari, 42, a jewellery designer (“RB Designs”) and donor guest. She says she admired the necklace but never touched it.
• Ramesh Bose, 50, the caterer for Heritage Night. He says he never left the banquet hall.

Most people suspect the night guard. When and how did the real necklace vanish, and who took it?

clue.label: The necklace
clue.title: The fake and the original
clue.text:
• The necklace in the case is lighter than the original. Its clasp is plain and modern.
• The catalogue photo of the original shows a clasp engraved with a small lion.
• The glass case is unbroken and locked.

questions.question: The case is intact and locked, yet the necklace inside is a fake. What does that say about the thief?
options: They broke in at night and replaced the glass before morning
They stood at the open case at some point, with a copy ready
They took it while the necklace was being moved between museums
They sold the museum a fake necklace in the first place

clue.label: Sketchbook
clue.title: A young visitor's drawing
clue.text:
A 10-year-old visitor drew the necklace on Saturday at 4 PM.
His sketch clearly shows the little lion on the clasp.

questions.question: A child's sketch is not expert evidence. Why is it still useful here?
options: Because children notice more than adults and never get details wrong
Because it proves the swap had already happened by Saturday
Because it shows the boy stood close enough to touch the necklace
Because it records a detail that only the real necklace has

clue.label: Cleaner's log
clue.title: Sunday morning
clue.text:
Sunday 8 AM — Imran cleaned the glass of the case.
He wrote: “Necklace sparkling nicely. The little lion is shining.”

questions.question: Put the sketch and the cleaner's note together. What do they narrow down?
options: The real necklace was still there at 8 AM on Sunday
The swap happened between Saturday 4 PM and Sunday 8 AM
Imran swapped the necklace while he was cleaning the glass
The necklace had been a fake since before Saturday

clue.label: Alarm and CCTV
clue.title: Sunday night
clue.text:
• No alarm rang.
• The gallery camera was off from 2 AM to 3 AM for routine maintenance.
• The case's lock sensor shows the case was not opened at any time between 9 PM on Sunday and 9 AM on Monday.

questions.question: The camera was off for an hour. Why is that hour NOT when the theft happened?
options: Because the night guard was awake and on his rounds
Because the camera would still have recorded the thief in the dark
Because the lock sensor shows the case stayed shut all night
Because thieves avoid a museum during maintenance work

clue.label: Key box
clue.title: When the case was opened
clue.text:
The case key stays in the curator's locked key box.
On Sunday the case was opened only once: at 7:15 PM, by the curator, to show the necklace to guests at Heritage Night (6 PM to 9 PM).

questions.question: The real necklace was there at 8 AM on Sunday and the case stayed shut all night. When was the swap?
options: During the cleaning at 8 AM on Sunday
Between 2 AM and 3 AM on Monday, while the gallery camera was off
On Monday morning, just before the museum opened
On Sunday evening, while the case was open for the guests

clue.label: Initials
clue.title: A mark on the fake
clue.text:
Tiny initials are stamped on the hinge of the fake: “R.B.”

Two of the people being talked about have these initials: Rekha Bhandari and Ramesh Bose.

questions.question: Two people share these initials. What is the sensible next step?
options: Arrest Rekha at once, because she is the one who makes jewellery
Arrest Ramesh at once, because caterers carry bags and boxes
Find out which R.B. could get near the open case on Sunday evening
Ignore the initials, since anyone could stamp two letters on a hinge

clue.label: Guest list
clue.title: Wristbands at Heritage Night
clue.text:
• Blue wristband: donors, allowed into the gallery. Rekha had a blue wristband.
• Green wristband: caterers, banquet hall only. Ramesh had a green wristband.
• A waiter: “The caterers stayed in the banquet hall. The corridor to the gallery needs a blue wristband.”

questions.question: What do the wristbands change?
options: Nothing: either R.B. could have walked into the gallery
They rule out one R.B., who could not enter the gallery
They rule out the donor, since donors were being watched
They show the waiter is covering for the caterers

clue.label: The guard
clue.title: Joseph Pinto
clue.text:
• In his locker: a loan recovery letter. He owes money.
• Patrol sheet: Joseph was at the main gate from 7 PM to 9 PM, signed by two colleagues.

questions.question: Most people suspect Joseph. What is the strongest point in his favour?
options: At the only time the case was open, two colleagues place him at the gate
He owes money, and people in debt are careful not to take risks
The camera was off at night, so nothing can be shown against him
He has guarded the museum for years without a single complaint

twist_md: New evidence has come in: statements from the curator and from another guest who was in the gallery.

clue.label: Curator's statement
clue.title: Fatima Sheikh
clue.text: “At 7:15 I unlocked the case so that Rekha and Mr. Anil could see the necklace up close. At 7:20 I stepped out for a phone call and was gone about five minutes. I relocked the case at 7:25.”

twist_questions.question: While the case was open, for how long was the necklace out of the curator's sight, and who was with it?
options: About five minutes; Rekha and Mr. Anil
About ten minutes; Rekha on her own
About five minutes; nobody at all
About two hours; all the guests at the party

clue.label: Guest's statement
clue.title: Mr. Anil Chopra, donor, 78
clue.text:
Mr. Anil has poor eyesight.

“Rekha held the necklace while Fatima was out. She turned her back to me.”

twist_questions.question: What does Mr. Anil's statement do to the case?
options: It clears Rekha, because he was standing beside her the whole time
It shows the curator lied about leaving for a phone call
It contradicts “never touched it” and gives a moment when no one saw her hands
It shows that Mr. Anil himself took the necklace home

clue.label: Guest's statement
clue.title: Later that evening
clue.text:
Mr. Anil: “Later that evening Rekha told me her studio is nearly bankrupt.”

The necklace is worth crores. A jeweller says a copy this good takes weeks to make.

twist_questions.question: What do “nearly bankrupt” and “weeks to make” tell us together?
options: It was a sudden temptation that came over a guest during the party
The curator had the copy made to claim the insurance money
The guard ordered the copy to pay off his loan
It was planned well ahead, by a skilled maker who needed money

answer.explanation: Rekha Bhandari swapped the real necklace for a replica she had made in advance (stamped R.B.) on Sunday evening, between 7:20 and 7:25 PM, while the curator was out on a phone call. She held the necklace with her back to Mr. Anil, who has poor eyesight, although she said she never touched it. The boy's Saturday sketch and the cleaner's Sunday 8 AM log show the real necklace, with its lion clasp, was there until Sunday. The case was not opened at night, so the camera gap is irrelevant. Ramesh Bose shares the initials but had a green wristband and could not enter the gallery. Joseph owes money but was at the main gate from 7 to 9 PM. Rekha's studio was nearly bankrupt.
